findings.title: Context's `config` ignores the copy that gets the readable schedule_type
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies `monitor.config` and replaces `schedule_type` with its display name (lines 160-162). Then it returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` at line 168, so the local `config` is never used and the event's `monitor` context carries the raw integer `schedule_type`. `get_schedule_type_display` is `ScheduleType.get_name(self.config["schedule_type"])` (src/sentry/monitors/models.py:344). The serializer (src/sentry/monitors/serializers.py:240-242) does use its copy. This bug existed before the PR and came along with the moved code. Since the function now lives in its own module, this is a cheap moment to return `config`. Doing so changes the context payload, so a test that asserts on the context would need updating.

findings.title: Moved docstring has typos and an example the function never produces
findings.body: "humam readible" should read "human readable". The examples "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected" don't match what the code returns. The code produces "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected" (line 150 and line 156), and its singular strings are status-specific, such as "A missed check-in was detected" (lines 123-127).

contracts.action: mark_failed now calls try_incident_threshold, which replaces the old in-file mark_failed_threshold
contracts.equivalent_path: The deleted mark_failed_threshold in mark_failed.py at the base commit
contracts.before_after: The body is identical apart from the renamed callee create_incident_occurrence. It does the same status check, the same threshold query with LIMIT through the queryset slice, the same get_or_create of MonitorIncident, the same mute check, and sends monitor_environment_failed afterwards. No other module imported mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, get_monitor_environment_context or SimpleCheckIn from mark_failed. The callers check_missed, check_timeout and monitor_consumer import only mark_failed. The tests patch sentry.issues.producer.produce_occurrence_to_kafka, which still resolves because the new module imports it locally.
contracts.visible_effect: No change. The same issue occurrences are produced to Kafka.
contracts.failure_mode: Unchanged. Exceptions propagate to the caller as before.

contracts.action: try_incident_threshold calls create_incident_occurrence for each failed check-in
contracts.before_after: The code moved verbatim. It imports IssueOccurrence and produce_occurrence_to_kafka locally, builds the same evidence and event_data, and adds the trace context. The loop is bounded by failure_issue_threshold, because previous_checkins is sliced before the id__in query.
contracts.visible_effect: The issue's title, evidence and tags are the same as before.
contracts.failure_mode: Unchanged. A Kafka produce error propagates.

summary: This PR is a pure refactor. It moves `mark_failed_threshold` into `incidents.py` as `try_incident_threshold`, and moves the occurrence helpers into `incident_occurrence.py`, renaming `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence`. `SimpleCheckIn` moves to `types.py`. The moved bodies are unchanged. No caller or test imported the moved symbols from `mark_failed`, and the test patches target `sentry.issues.producer`, which still resolves. The new imports don't create an import cycle. Two optional notes, both on code that existed before the PR: `get_monitor_environment_context` throws away its schedule_type-formatted config copy, and the `get_failure_reason` docstring has typos and examples the function never produces.
